payload.title: Geometry study: NACA 0012 finite wing
abstract: We took NACA 0012 finite wing through surface check, meshing, and a steady solve to establish whether the chain yields a trustworthy force.
The mesh reached 140,580 cells at max non-orthogonality 40.5° and max skewness 1.93; drag settled at 0.01205 ± 3.4e-07.
Rebased onto the published area basis that is 0.0121 against 0.009 from Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 0012 section data.
methods: Surface intake and check on NACA 0012 finite wing.
Meshed to 140,580 cells; quality gated at 70° non-orthogonality and 4 skewness.
300 steady iterations on the gated mesh.
Forces averaged over the final fifth of the iteration history; the band is the spread of that window.

results.envelope: max non-orthogonality 40.5° vs 70° gate (pass), max skewness 1.93 vs 4.0 guidance (pass)

uncertainty: Reported band: settling spread of the coefficient over the averaging window, a floor, not a bound.

Numerical uncertainty from a 3-mesh refinement study: ±0.015 on Cd; 3-mesh study (r = 1.28), observed order p = 3.17; least-squares fit with safety factor 1.25 (Eca and Hoekstra 2014); observed order limited to the theoretical range (band uses p = 2.5).

Compared against Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 0012 section data: measured Cd 0.012 is 34% from Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959), NACA 0012 section data, Cd 0.009, outside the ±30% band.
